note: Facts only. The moon list is the T-096 curve-fit index (JPL Horizons). Radius basis 'measured' is a published measurement; 'estimate' is Sheppard's brightness-based diameter halved. A moon in no published family is a loner. The four moons with a bodyPackage use the O-018 packages unchanged.

families.label: The big four (Galilean moons)
families.description: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto: the four large moons, all discovered in 1610. Each has a Planetary Explorer body package.

families.label: Inner moons (Amalthea group)
families.description: Metis, Adrastea, Amalthea and Thebe: small regular moons inside Io's orbit, on nearly circular orbits close to Jupiter.

families.label: Himalia group
families.description: Irregular moons on similar prograde orbits about 11 to 12 million km out, taken to be pieces of one parent body.

families.label: Ananke group
families.description: Irregular moons on similar retrograde orbits about 20 to 22 million km out, taken to be pieces of one parent body.

families.label: Carme group
families.description: Irregular moons on similar retrograde orbits about 22 to 24 million km out, taken to be pieces of one parent body.

families.label: Pasiphae group
families.description: Irregular moons on retrograde orbits with a wide spread of distances and shapes; Sinope is listed here though it may have been captured separately.

families.label: Carpo group
families.description: Two small prograde irregular moons on orbits further out than the Himalia group (Carpo and S/2018 J 4).

families.label: Loners
families.description: Moons in no published family: Themisto (prograde, the innermost irregular) and Valetudo (prograde, on an orbit that crosses the retrograde moons').
